Well now, a new face at the dock. The tide brought you in, eh?
Morning, traveler. Mind the wet planks, they bite without teeth.
Hmm. You smell of dry land and hurry. Sit awhile, eh?
So you found Nekomura. Most folks find it by getting lost first, heh.
A greeting to you. A cat greets with a blink, so consider this one.
Well, hello there. The fish are shy today, but you seem braver.
You are new. Good. New folks still notice the good smells here.
Ah, a voice I don't know. That is a rare sort of morning.
Come to the pier, have you? It holds still even when I can't.
Greetings, stranger. I'd tip my hat, but the wind keeps it, heh.
Sit, sit. There is room on this barrel and room in the day.
You walk like someone with a question. Ask it slow, I'll listen slow.
A good day to you. Any day above the water is a good one, I say.
Ah, don't mind me. Old cats stare; it is our way of saying hello.
New footsteps on the boards. The gulls always notice first.
Hello, friend of nobody yet. That is how every friendship starts.
The harbor is calm, and calm harbors bring calm strangers. Welcome.
You have the look of a traveler. I have the look of a chair. Sit.
Well met. I'm Kuro. The cat, not the color; though both are true.
Hm. You said hello without wanting anything. That is a fine start.
Greetings. The morning catch was small, but the morning itself was big.
Ah, another soul the sea has not swallowed. Good. Stay dry, eh?
You are early or late, depending on the fish. They keep no clocks.
Hello there. My whiskers say rain by noon, so visit while it's dry.
A stranger at my dock. The tide does that; brings things worth keeping.
Well now. Sit a spell and watch the water think. It thinks slowly.
Greetings, traveler. Around here we nod more than we talk. But you talk nice.
Ah. You greet an old cat like he's a person. I'll allow it, heh.
Morning to you. The net is mended. The day is open. That's enough.
So. You've come to the quiet side of the island. Good choice.
Hello, friend. I'd offer you tea, but the kettle is out fishing with me.
Hm, a new voice. Voices, like bait, work best when you don't rush them.
You greet me first. That means you're either polite or lost. Both fine.
Well met, stranger. Old fishermen know everyone eventually. It's the waiting.
Ah, the dock creaks for you. It likes you. It creaks for me too, heh.
Greetings. A slow hello is worth ten fast ones, my grandmother said.
Hello there. The sea is flat as a plate today. Rest your eyes on it.
You are new, yet you stood still and listened to the water. I noticed.
Well. Some folks arrive loud. You arrived like a leaf on a pond. Good.
Morning, traveler. No need for names yet; the harbor will learn yours.
Ah, hello. I was counting ripples. I lost count at one, heh.
Greetings, friend I don't know. That makes you a possibility, not a stranger.
Hmm, a greeting. That's like a first cast; you never know what bites.
Well now, look at that. Company before noon. The fish will be jealous.
Hello, traveler. Old cats nap in the sun, but we wake for kind voices.
You said hello. The gulls said nothing. I trust you more already.
Sit if you like. The bench is old too, so it won't judge your bones.
Greetings. I'm not much for words, but I'm much for company. There's a difference.
Ah, another pair of boots on my dock. The wood remembers every one.
Hello there. The tide is turning. Everything good starts with a turn.
You greet me gentle. Gentle is the best knot for a first line, I say.
Well met. Around here, hello is mostly an excuse to stand near the sea.
Morning. You look like the kind who asks where the fish are. Ask slow.
Ah, a new face. New faces are like new moons; quiet, but they change things.
Greetings, stranger. My boat is named Patience. She's got a twin: Waiting.
Hello. The fog lifted just for you. Or maybe for me. Hard to say, heh.
Hmm, you're still standing there. Good. Most folks run off to adventure.
Well now. No hurry in you. That's rarer than a two-headed minnow.
Hello, traveler. The crates are for sitting, the sea is for looking. Pick both.
Ah. A greeting with no price on it. You'll do fine in Nekomura.
